Thanks for the call earlier. Our InfoSec team asked for a concise architecture overview showing how tenant traffic is isolated for your Dedicated and Private deployment options. Specifically they asked: 
- Is there a bump-in-the-wire proxy per-tenant or shared?
- How is egress controlled and audited (per-tenant egress NAT, central egress proxy, or customer-managed gateway)?
- How are east-west calls between model-serving instances prevented from touching other tenants' KV caches?
- Any packet-level filtering or SR-IOV/PCI passthrough notes we can include in our SIG/SOC2 review?

Can you share a short diagram + a bulleted explanation suitable for the SOC2 auditor? We are on a tight timeline for our internal SIG review by 08/28.

Natalie —

High level summary attached and pasted below. I've kept it auditor-friendly (diagram + short bullets). Short answers up front:
- Bump-in-the-wire model: per-tenant overlay with a dedicated tenant proxy process (shared host, logically isolated) by default for Redwood Dedicated; for Private deployments customers can opt for customer-managed gateway (we provide the proxy container image).
- Egress: Centralized egress proxy per-region per-customer with per-tenant flow tagging and logs. We support optional per-tenant NAT if the customer requests static IPs.
- East-west isolation: KV caches are namespaced and enforced at the runtime shim; network policies prevent tenant traffic from reaching other tenant proxies.
- Hardware isolation: SR-IOV VF assignment is used for high-performance Dedicated pools when requested; otherwise we rely on strict linux namespaces + eBPF/XDP filtering.

I'll put a draw.io PNG in the next message with callouts.

Action items: I will: 1) attach the diagram, 2) include an excerpt of the egress proxy config and log format for auditor review.

-aditya
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Team —

Draft artifacts for Acme (SIG/SOC2). Please review for accuracy and call out anything we should not share verbatim. I attached:
- redwood-tenant-overlay-v1.drawio.png (annotated diagram)
- egress-proxy-config-excerpt.txt (sanitized config showing per-tenant tagging)
- segmentation-table-v2.csv (table mapping tenant components to controls)

Key diagram callouts to validate:
1) Tenant overlay network: VXLAN overlay per-customer; each tenant has an overlay subnet and a tenant proxy (containerized) that terminates TLS for downstream model-worker connections.
2) Bump-in-the-wire proxy: the proxy performs tenant-aware routing, per-request policy enforcement, and injects a tenant identifier into the request header (for auditing).
3) Egress control: all outbound traffic flows through the egress proxy chain (region-level egress cluster) which emits structured JSON logs to our logging pipeline (indexed by tenant_id). Static egress IP requested by tenant will instantiate a NAT allocation in the same egress cluster.
4) East-west separation: model-serving processes use a namespaced KV store; cross-tenant access is blocked by the runtime's ACLs. Network policies (CNI + eBPF) and the overlay prevent packet-level cross-tenant forwarding.
5) Hardware mode: when customers request dedicated NICs (SR-IOV), the tenant proxy gets a VF and we disable host-level NF tables for passthrough performance; that VF allocation is audited at provisioning time.

Please review and reply by EOD so I can send to Natalie.

Thanks,
Aditya
